Woot (which is owned by Amazon) is offering a rare discount on a Switch 2 for Black Friday. While supplies last, you can pick up a grade A refurbished Nintendo Switch 2 console for just $409 after $40 off coupon code " BIGFRIDAY ". First time new customers can get it for $389 after $60 off discount using the same code. Amazon Prime members get free delivery, otherwise add $5 shipping. This system comes with a 90-day Woot warranty.

Save $90 to $110 Off the Nintendo Switch 2 Console

Grade A refurbished

According to Woot:

Hey, you there! This item has been inspected and guaranteed to have minimal cosmetic damage & has successfully passed a full diagnostic test which ensures like-new functionality & removal of any prior-user's personal information. Unit includes OEM accessories and is packaged in a generic white or brown box.

Alternatively, save $50 Off the Nintendo Switch 2 Mario Kart World console bundle

Alternatively, you can save $50 off the official Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 console bundle, which includes a copy of Mario Kart World and 3 months of Nintendo Switch Online membership. This may end up being the better deal if you end up purchasing Mario Kart World anyways, and you'll also be getting the 1 year Nintendo warranty.

At this point, upgrading from the Switch is totally worth it

The Nintendo Switch 2 console first released back in June of 2025 at a starting MSRP of $450. After the recent Nintendo price hike, the price went up to $500. At this point, upgrading from the Switch to the Switch 2 is a no-brainer. Several Switch 2 exclusives have been released including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, Pokemon Pokopia, Kirby Air Riders, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and more. Zelda: Ocarina of Time scored a 9/10 from IGN's Logan Plant.

Triple-A ports have also made their way to the Switch 2 console, including Cyberpunk 2077 and Final Fantasy VII Remake, making the Switch 2 a veritable competitor to pricier handheld gaming PCs. The Switch 2 hardware is powerful enough to run these games at a very playable clip, a feat that's impossible on the original Switch's hardware.
